words.sense: Stubbornly resisting instructions, cooperation, or attempts to change.
misconceptions: Feeling uncertain does not amount to defiance.

words.sense: Hesitant or unwilling, without necessarily defying a request.
misconceptions: Quietly delaying a choice is not necessarily fighting directions.

semantic_axes.description: Defiant noncooperation versus hesitation without entrenched resistance.

edges.boundary_rule: Recalcitrant describes persistent defiance of direction; reluctant describes unwillingness or hesitation that need not become defiance.

misconceptions.M1: Treats hesitation or discomfort as active defiance.
misconceptions.M2: Treats repeated rejection of an instruction as mere nervousness.
misconceptions.M3: Confuses eventual cooperation with ongoing opposition to authority.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Noor’s response to joining the school play?

beats.text: Noor looks at the audition sheet several times and says she worries about forgetting lines, but eventually signs up.
beats.reason: The first detail establishes uneasiness ends in voluntary participation; that is the meaningful distinction.

beats.text: She asks for a small role at first and attends practice as promised.
beats.decisive_clue: continued cooperation despite preference for a small role
beats.reason: The new detail confirms continued cooperation despite preference for a small role and rules out the competing sense.

chains.feedback_short: She joins and practices despite her worry; she does not defy instructions.
chains.feedback_deep: Recalcitrant means defiantly resistant to direction. Reluctant means hesitant or unwilling. Here, worry before joining is hesitancy; she does not dig in against directions.
chains.contrast_rule: Reluctance hesitates; recalcitrance digs in against direction.

hints.attention: Look at what happens after the initial hesitation.
hints.axis: Defiant noncooperation versus hesitation without entrenched resistance.
hints.contrast: Reluctance hesitates; recalcitrance digs in against direction.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Idris’s response to the coach’s instruction?

beats.text: The coach asks Idris three times to put his phone away; Idris keeps scrolling and says, “You cannot make me.”
beats.decisive_clue: open defiance continues despite repeated direct instructions
beats.reason: The first detail establishes open defiance continues despite repeated direct instructions; that is the meaningful distinction.

beats.text: Even when the rest of the group starts the drill, he keeps the phone out and ignores the coach.
beats.decisive_clue: the same defiance persists when practice begins
beats.reason: The deciding fact remains open defiance continues despite repeated direct instructions; the added detail does not change that.

chains.feedback_short: The repeated instructions and his refusal to comply decide the word.
chains.feedback_deep: Recalcitrant means defiantly resistant to direction. Reluctant means hesitant or unwilling. Here, this is resistance to being told what to do, not merely uncertainty about a task.
chains.contrast_rule: Reluctance hesitates; recalcitrance digs in against direction.

hints.attention: Does he hesitate, or challenge the instruction itself?
hints.axis: Defiant noncooperation versus hesitation without entrenched resistance.
hints.contrast: Reluctance hesitates; recalcitrance digs in against direction.

beats.reason: The first detail establishes a person rejects an agreed responsibility despite a reminder; that is the meaningful distinction.

beats.text: After two house meetings asking him to follow the arrangement, he writes, “I won’t do it,” across the schedule.
beats.decisive_clue: he keeps opposing repeated attempts to enforce the same agreement
beats.reason: The new detail confirms he keeps opposing repeated attempts to enforce the same agreement and rules out the competing sense.

chains.feedback_short: Repeated resistance to the same agreed duty is the deciding fact.
chains.feedback_deep: Recalcitrant means defiantly resistant to direction. Reluctant means hesitant or unwilling. Here, persistent noncooperation despite direct requests goes beyond ordinary hesitation.

beats.text: When asked three times to staff that same desk, she pushes its sign away and says, “I won’t follow your orders.”

beats.reason: The new evidence establishes active refusal of repeated instructions about that same task, so the other word now fits the same subject better.

chains.feedback_short: Repeatedly rejecting the assigned duty turns initial hesitation into defiance.

chains.feedback_short: He tastes the dish despite caution; there is no defiant opposition.
chains.feedback_deep: Recalcitrant means defiantly resistant to direction. Reluctant means hesitant or unwilling. Here, the hesitation is about his own uncertainty, not entrenched resistance to authority.
